requiredFindings.title: Define how blind results survive ordinary regeneration and remain bound to the reviewed inputs
requiredFindings.finding: The plan replaces outstanding held-out rows in the shared generated census, but gives no ordinary-mode preservation/checking rule. At the pinned product base, census_output always emits outstanding rows for held-outs and heldOutMargin=outstanding; main --check compares the entire regenerated file byte for byte, while --write replaces it. Thus the specified blind run makes the retained ordinary census --check fail, and an ordinary regeneration erases its result. Blind rows also omit raw costs, so they cannot simply be carried across a changed manifest, model/closure or cap profile and still establish the current margin. The plan does not state the binding/invalidation rule or how the top-level state and failure list are reconciled with its instruction to write only held-out rows.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Specify a reviewed blind-result lifecycle: how the ordinary mode validates/preserves or separately composes the authorized result without opening held-out stores; which exact reviewed manifest, model/tool, cost-closure, caps and root-length inputs the receipt binds; and when drift invalidates the result or requires a newly reviewed run. Define the permitted top-level updates (heldOutMargin and failure/cap state) and keep all lead-readable/workspace evidence unchanged except such explicit updates. Add synthetic controls for blind run followed by ordinary --check/regeneration, input drift, and forbidden ordinary held-out access. Metadata binding can use existing public pins and must not add content-bearing output.

requiredFindings.title: Define error rows and require complete successful coverage before declaring the margin held
requiredFindings.finding: The allowed row fields and classification describe computed margins, but INTEGRITY, POPULATION, MODEL and IO failures can occur before any margins exist. The plan nevertheless says every failure becomes a class and a failing row has its margins only. It does not define where the class goes, whether unavailable margins are absent/null, or the exact success rule for integrity/population failure versus a genuine low margin. Its margin-only passes2x equivalence applies to successful measurements, not errored or missing rows. Without explicit row variants and exact held-out-ID coverage, the after-run test could accept high/stale margin values despite a failed verification, or overlook an omitted/duplicated entry. Existing listed controls do not cover MODEL/IO failures or these aggregate-state cases.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Define a closed success-row and error-row format. Successful measurements require passed integrity/population checks and three valid margins; error rows emit only the manifest ID, false/error status and an allowed class, with no fabricated margins or exception text. Define passes2x from the margins only for successful measurements, and require exactly one successful passing row for every expected held-out ID before heldOutMargin can become holds. Define failure versus incomplete/error top-level states and keep the completion gate open for either. Extend synthetic canary/output allow-list controls to MODEL and IO errors, absent/duplicate/unknown IDs, and failure rows carrying misleading margin values; capture stdout and stderr as well as saved output.

nonBlockingObservations.location: PLAN-r5.md r5 changes quotation; REQUEST.md Bases
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The plan labels its selected-option quotation verbatim but omits the owner-record option text's opening Authorize and capitalizes the following article. Preserve the full option text or label this an excerpt. The request also describes the exact bases as inventory v195/shared r95, while those hashes are inventory v198/shared r98. The subject manifest pins and the staged plan's historical-base labels are consistent; these are presentation corrections.
